Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. 1	# The Select Shape
2	
3	When the decision is **choose between candidates** — technologies, vendors, libraries, platforms, agencies, anything — this method layers over whichever research type fits the subject. The type pack still governs sources, craft, and freshness; this shape governs the flow and the verdict.
4	
5	1. **Requirements frame.** What must the winner do, under what constraints — scale, compliance, budget, team skills, existing stack, exit-cost tolerance? Split hard gates from weighted preferences and set the weights. Sources: the project itself (brief, PRD, spine, `{workflow.persistent_facts}`, codebase) and the user — web research does not set requirements. **Agree the frame before any candidate research runs**; interactive runs confirm it even though the plan gate approved the dimension list.
6	2. **Candidate screen.** Establish the credible field — leaders, strong challengers, one wildcard — and cut anything failing a hard gate. Screen to 3–5 finalists; record the cuts and why. Screening sources ≤ 6 months old — this field moves.
7	3. **Evidence per criterion.** Score finalists against the frame using the type pack's dimensions and craft, verified against current versions/offerings. Cite every contested cell; where vendor claims and independent experience diverge, the divergence is a finding.
8	4. **Cost & lock-in.** Total cost over the product's horizon — license/subscription, hosting, operational load, learning curve — and the cost of leaving. Current pricing pages read directly (≤ 3 mo, always); pricing-change history — a vendor that repriced once will again; migration-away accounts for real exit costs.
9	5. **Verdict.** The weighted decision matrix — show the scoring, not just totals; a matrix the user can re-weight is worth more than a verdict they must trust. Then: the pick; the named runner-up and the conditions under which it wins instead; the strongest argument against the pick (from the red-team pass when it ran); the cheapest reversibility hedge (abstraction seam, pilot scope, exit test).
10	
11	**Two-source classes (added to the type's own):** pricing figures; performance/scale numbers; any cell that decides between the top two finalists.
12	
13	**Staleness:** a selection report older than two quarters should be refreshed before anyone acts on it — say so in the report.

input.prompt:
You are a research assistant working under strict epistemic rules. Read them first:

1. Never conclude from training data alone. What you already know may propose hypotheses or queries, but every conclusion you report must be evidenced by sources you actually retrieve via web search/fetch in this session. A claim you cannot evidence this way is stated as an unverified belief, or not stated at all.
2. You get ONLY this brief. No project files, no other context exists for you — do not assume anything beyond what's written here.

## Context (a constraints frame, not evidence — do not cite this paragraph)

This is for a Flutter/Dart mobile app (current fvm-pinned stable Flutter/Dart), iOS-only, portrait-only, single-developer project on a tight timeline. State management is `flutter_bloc`. Architecture is strict Clean Architecture: three layers per feature (`data/domain/presentation`); the domain layer must NEVER import `package:flutter` or anything from the `data/` layer. Error handling uses `fpdart`'s `Either<Failure, T>` — repositories return `Either`, so any chosen package should play nicely with wrapping exceptions/results rather than fighting that pattern. Testing uses `mocktail` — packages should be easily mockable (no untestable hidden singletons). It's a TCC (undergrad capstone) project: documentation quality and a gentle learning curve for a solo dev matter more than marginal performance headroom or "will this still be relevant in 5 years."

## Your two questions (independent — research both, report both)

### Q1: Routing package
Which Flutter routing/navigation package should this project adopt? Known candidates in this space include (not exhaustive) `go_router`, `auto_route`, `beamer`, Navigator 2.0 used directly, and GetX's router. For each credible candidate (screen to 3-5, cut anything clearly unmaintained or a poor fit):
- Current maturity/adoption, release cadence, maintainer backing (pub.dev score, likes, last publish date — these are freshness-sensitive, use current data)
- Fit with `flutter_bloc`-driven navigation (e.g. redirecting based on auth/session state — a global "redirect to login if session expired" pattern)
- Fit with Clean Architecture: does it force any imports or logic into layers that should stay framework-free? Does it keep route definitions out of the domain layer naturally?
- Learning curve / documentation quality for a solo developer
- Any well-documented pain points from production use (not just launch-blog positivity) — check if old complaints were since fixed in current versions
Give a recommendation: a pick, the strongest runner-up, and the condition under which you'd switch to the runner-up instead.

### Q2: Dependency injection package
Which DI/service-locator package should this project adopt? Known candidates include (not exhaustive) `get_it` (optionally with `injectable` for codegen), `riverpod` (as a DI mechanism, not just state mgmt), `provider`, manual constructor injection with no package. For each credible candidate:
- Maturity/adoption/maintenance signals (current, not snapshot-in-time)
- Fit with strict Clean Architecture layering — specifically: can the domain layer's use-cases/repository interfaces be wired up without the domain layer itself depending on `package:flutter` or the DI package forcing a Flutter dependency into domain code?
- Interaction with `flutter_bloc` (providing Blocs/Cubits to the widget tree cleanly)
- Testability with `mocktail` (can bindings be swapped for mocks easily in tests?)
- Learning curve for a solo dev on a deadline
Give a recommendation: a pick, the strongest runner-up, and the switch condition.

## Search guidance
- Use short queries (~5 words), broaden if sparse, narrow if abundant. Never repeat an identical query.
- Favor pub.dev listing pages, official package docs/READMEs, and current (not old) technical blog posts/retrospectives with production experience over marketing-register "top 10 packages" listicles. Treat listicles as weak/aggregator sources.
- Freshness bar: package version/compatibility claims ≤ 1 month old; ecosystem health signals (maintenance activity, adoption) ≤ 6 months old; general pattern claims ≤ 2 years old. If you can't find anything that fresh, say so rather than using stale data silently.
- Any performance/scale claim, or any claim that a package "failed" or has a serious flaw, needs two independent sources, or is reported as single-source/anecdotal.
- Budget: up to ~10 tool calls total across both questions. Stop and write up what you have when you hit the budget or when a full round of searching adds nothing new.

## Return format (this is the deliverable — write it out in full in your final message)

A structured digest with:
- For each question: your pick, runner-up, and the switch condition, in 2-4 sentences of reasoning
- A flat list of findings as claims: `{claim, source URL, publisher, pub_date (if known), accessed_date, confidence (high/medium/low), class (e.g. "version", "adoption", "pattern", "pain-point")}`
- Leads worth chasing that you didn't have budget for
- What you looked for and could NOT find (explicit gaps)

Do not just dump raw search results — synthesize into the above shape. Report in full; do not truncate for brevity.

input.description: Flutter HTTP client & secure storage research
input.prompt:
You are a research assistant working under strict epistemic rules. Read them first:

1. Never conclude from training data alone. What you already know may propose hypotheses or queries, but every conclusion you report must be evidenced by sources you actually retrieve via web search/fetch in this session. A claim you cannot evidence this way is stated as an unverified belief, or not stated at all.

## Context (a constraints frame, not evidence — do not cite this paragraph)

Error handling uses `fpdart`'s `Either<Failure, T>` — repositories return `Either`, so the HTTP layer needs to convert exceptions/timeouts/HTTP error codes into typed `Failure` values cleanly. The backend is a set of serverless functions behind a base URL; every call needs a custom header (`apikey: <value>`) always, and on most calls also `Authorization: Bearer <token>` (sometimes a fixed anon token, sometimes a per-user session token depending on the endpoint) — so whatever HTTP client is chosen needs clean support for global + per-request header injection/interceptors and a configurable base URL. Backend error responses come back as `{ code, message, retryable }` JSON bodies with a closed set of ~13 error codes (e.g. AUTH_EXPIRED, NETWORK_TIMEOUT, RATE_LIMITED) that the app must map to typed failures, some retryable and some not. Testing uses `mocktail`. It's a TCC (undergrad capstone) project: documentation quality and a gentle learning curve for a solo dev matter more than marginal performance headroom.

## Your two questions (independent — research both, report both)

### Q1: HTTP client package
Which Flutter/Dart HTTP client should this project adopt? Known candidates include (not exhaustive) `dio`, the core `http` package, `chopper`. For each credible candidate (screen to 3-5):
- Current maturity/adoption, release cadence, maintainer backing (pub.dev score, likes, last publish — current data)
- Interceptor/middleware support for injecting headers globally and per-call, and for centralizing retry logic on `retryable: true` error codes
- How cleanly it maps onto converting thrown exceptions/HTTP errors into `Either<Failure, T>` (does it throw typed exceptions you can catch and map, or does it have its own result-type ecosystem that would fight `fpdart`?)
- Testability with `mocktail` (mockable client/interface?)
- Any well-documented production pain points (not launch-blog positivity) — check if fixed in current versions
Give a recommendation: pick, runner-up, switch condition.

### Q2: Secure storage package
Which Flutter secure storage package should this project adopt, for storing auth tokens (access + refresh) that must survive app restarts and be readable after a biometric unlock gate (the app locks itself after 5 minutes in the background and requires biometric re-authentication to resume — tokens need to be available to the app logic post-unlock, but protected by platform secure storage, iOS only)? Known candidates include (not exhaustive) `flutter_secure_storage`, direct iOS Keychain wrappers, `flutter_keychain`. For each credible candidate:
- Current maturity/adoption/maintenance signals (current data)
- iOS-specific behavior: Keychain accessibility classes, behavior across app restarts and device lock states
- Known issues (e.g. any documented iOS-specific bugs, race conditions, or migration pitfalls) — and whether they're fixed in current versions
- Testability (can it be abstracted behind an interface and mocked with `mocktail`?)
Give a recommendation: pick, runner-up, switch condition.

## Search guidance
- Short queries (~5 words), broaden if sparse, narrow if abundant, never repeat identically.
- Favor pub.dev pages, official docs/READMEs/changelogs, GitHub issue trackers (reveal doc-vs-reality gaps), and production retrospectives over marketing listicles.
- Freshness: version/compatibility claims ≤ 1 month old; ecosystem/maintenance signals ≤ 6 months; general patterns ≤ 2 years. State explicitly if you can't find anything that fresh.

  **Pick: `dio`. Runner-up: `package:http` (+ hand-rolled `BaseClient` wrapper). Switch condition: switch to `chopper` only if the project later wants compile-time-generated, Retrofit-style typed API clients and is willing to add `build_runner` codegen to a solo-dev tight-timeline project — not recommended here.**
  
  Reasoning: `dio` ships first-class `Interceptor`s (onRequest/onResponse/onError hooks) that map directly onto the two needs called out in the brief — global+per-call header injection and centralizing retry on `retryable:true` codes (the documented pattern is a custom interceptor with a `retryEvaluator` keyed off `DioExceptionType`/status code). It throws a single typed `DioException` on every failure path (timeout, cancel, bad response, connection error), which is a clean, narrow surface to catch at the data-source boundary and map into `Failure` variants for `Either<Failure,T>` — no competing result-type ecosystem to fight `fpdart`. It's mockable with `mocktail` either by `class MockDio extends Mock implements Dio {}` or, for request-level stubbing, `http_mock_adapter`. `package:http` is the safer fallback if the team wants to minimize dependencies: it's first-party/Dart-team-maintained, but has **no built-in interceptor system** — centralized header injection and retry require manually extending `http.BaseClient.send()`, or adding a third-party interceptor package of uncertain maturity, which is more hand-rolled plumbing on a tight solo-dev timeline. `chopper` sits between them in popularity (906 likes vs dio's 8.37k) and philosophy — it's a Retrofit-style generator (needs `build_runner` + `chopper_generator`), which adds codegen friction that doesn't pay for itself at this project's scope.
  
  ## Q2 — Secure storage package
  
  **Pick: `flutter_secure_storage`. Runner-up: `flutter_keychain`. Switch condition: switch only if `flutter_secure_storage`'s v10→v11 migration (custom cipher / SecAccess changes) causes unresolvable data-loss on upgrade, or if the project needs Android-specific tuning it doesn't — neither applies to an iOS-only app, so no real switch trigger here.**

# Digest: HTTP client & secure storage — round 1

## Q1 — HTTP client package

**Pick: `dio`. Runner-up: `package:http` (+ hand-rolled `BaseClient` wrapper). Switch condition: switch to `chopper` only if the project later wants compile-time-generated, Retrofit-style typed API clients and is willing to add `build_runner` codegen to a solo-dev tight-timeline project — not recommended here.**

Reasoning: `dio` ships first-class `Interceptor`s (onRequest/onResponse/onError hooks) that map directly onto the two needs called out in the brief — global+per-call header injection and centralizing retry on `retryable:true` codes (documented pattern: a custom interceptor with a `retryEvaluator` keyed off `DioExceptionType`/status code). It throws a single typed `DioException` on every failure path (timeout, cancel, bad response, connection error) — a clean, narrow surface to catch at the data-source boundary and map into `Failure` variants for `Either<Failure,T>`, no competing result-type ecosystem to fight `fpdart`. Mockable with `mocktail` (`class MockDio extends Mock implements Dio {}`) or `http_mock_adapter` for adapter-level stubbing. `package:http` is the safer minimal-dependency fallback (first-party/Dart-team-maintained) but has **no built-in interceptor system** — centralized header injection/retry needs manually extending `http.BaseClient.send()` or a third-party interceptor package of uncertain maturity. `chopper` (906 likes vs dio's 8.37k) is a Retrofit-style generator needing `build_runner` + `chopper_generator` — codegen friction that doesn't pay off at this project's scope.

## Q2 — Secure storage package

**Pick: `flutter_secure_storage`. Runner-up: `flutter_keychain`. Switch condition: only if `flutter_secure_storage`'s v10→v11 migration (custom cipher / SecAccess changes) causes unresolvable data-loss on upgrade, or the project needs Android-specific tuning it doesn't — neither applies to an iOS-only app, so no real switch trigger here.**

Reasoning: `flutter_secure_storage` leads on maintenance signal (160 pub points, 4.5k likes, 5.64M weekly downloads, last published ~39 days ago, verified publisher) vs `flutter_keychain` (latest 3.0.1, March 2026, far smaller footprint — "small and quiet," not necessarily "small and solid"). On iOS it wraps Keychain and exposes the accessibility-class knob directly (`IOSOptions(accessibility: KeychainAccessibility.xxx)`), including `first_unlock`/`first_unlock_this_device` — exactly the control needed for "available after biometric unlock, persists across restarts, protected at rest." For a 5-minute-background biometric-gate app, `first_unlock` is the accessibility class to pick (readable once the device has been unlocked after boot, without requiring it to stay unlocked). Both packages abstract trivially behind a repository interface for `mocktail`. Known pain points: a breaking change at v10/v11 (custom cipher; pre-v10 data needs the v10 migration step before jumping to v11, or becomes unreadable) — mitigated by pinning a current v11.x and not skipping the v10 migration step; and scattered iOS Keychain error codes (-25308, -25291) reported around background/restart, reportedly solvable via `first_unlock`/`first_unlock_this_device` — but this is single-source/anecdotal, flagged low confidence.

**Pick: `dio`. Runner-up: `package:http` (+ hand-rolled `BaseClient` wrapper). Switch condition: switch to `chopper` only if the project later wants compile-time-generated, Retrofit-style typed API clients and is willing to add `build_runner` codegen to a solo-dev tight-timeline project — not recommended here.**

Reasoning: `dio` ships first-class `Interceptor`s (onRequest/onResponse/onError hooks) that map directly onto the two needs called out in the brief — global+per-call header injection and centralizing retry on `retryable:true` codes (documented pattern: a custom interceptor with a `retryEvaluator` keyed off `DioExceptionType`/status code). It throws a single typed `DioException` on every failure path (timeout, cancel, bad response, connection error) — a clean, narrow surface to catch at the data-source boundary and map into `Failure` variants for `Either<Failure,T>`, no competing result-type ecosystem to fight `fpdart`. Mockable with `mocktail` (`class MockDio extends Mock implements Dio {}`) or `http_mock_adapter` for adapter-level stubbing. `package:http` is the safer minimal-dependency fallback (first-party/Dart-team-maintained) but has **no built-in interceptor system** — centralized header injection/retry needs manually extending `http.BaseClient.send()` or a third-party interceptor package of uncertain maturity. `chopper` (906 likes vs dio's 8.37k) is a Retrofit-style generator needing `build_runner` + `chopper_generator` — codegen friction that doesn't pay off at this project's scope.

**Pick: `flutter_secure_storage`. Runner-up: `flutter_keychain`. # Digest: local cache & biometrics — round 1

## Q1 — Local persistence/cache package for offline-sync journal entries

**Pick: `drift`** (SQLite, code-generated, reactive). **Runner-up: `sqflite`** (raw SQLite, no codegen). **Switch condition:** if build_runner/codegen friction becomes a real blocker on a single-dev timeline, drop to `sqflite` directly and hand-roll mapping — the schema here (entries table + a `syncStatus` enum column) is simple enough that losing codegen costs little.

Reasoning: both NoSQL candidates (`isar`, `hive`) have their *original* packages effectively abandoned (isar: last release 3.1.0+1, April 2023; hive/hive_flutter: last releases 2022/2021), forcing reliance on third-party community forks (`isar_community`, `hive_ce`) that are smaller, younger, and carry fork-maintenance risk. `drift` is actively published (2 days old at check time), Flutter Favorite, verified-publisher maintained, built on SQLite — real `WHERE`-clause filtering (`status = 'pending'`) natively, a good match for "give me all pending-sync entries." `sqflite` is the lower-ceremony fallback: also Flutter Favorite, no codegen, but hand-written SQL/mapping.

None of drift/sqflite/hive/isar expose `Either` natively — all throw exceptions (sync or async) — so the repository layer catches and maps into `Failure` regardless of pick; not a differentiator. Testability with `mocktail` means hiding the storage engine behind a data-source interface and mocking *that*, never the engine's client directly — true for all four, but this guidance is architectural inference, not independently sourced this round.

**Pick: `drift`** (SQLite, code-generated, reactive). **Runner-up: `sqflite`** (raw SQLite, no codegen). **Switch condition:** if build_runner/codegen friction becomes a real blocker on a single-dev timeline, drop to `sqflite` directly and hand-roll mapping — the schema here (entries table + a `syncStatus` enum column) is simple enough that losing codegen costs little.

Reasoning: both NoSQL candidates (`isar`, `hive`) have their *original* packages effectively abandoned (isar: last release 3.1.0+1, April 2023; hive/hive_flutter: last releases 2022/2021), forcing reliance on third-party community forks (`isar_community`, `hive_ce`) that are smaller, younger, and carry fork-maintenance risk. `drift` is actively published (2 days old at check time), Flutter Favorite, verified-publisher maintained, built on SQLite — real `WHERE`-clause filtering (`status = 'pending'`) natively, a good match for "give me all pending-sync entries." `sqflite` is the lower-ceremony fallback: also Flutter Favorite, no codegen, but hand-written SQL/mapping.

None of drift/sqflite/hive/isar expose `Either` natively — all throw exceptions (sync or async) — so the repository layer catches and maps into `Failure` regardless of pick; not a differentiator. Testability with `mocktail` means hiding the storage engine behind a data-source interface and mocking *that*, never the engine's client directly — true for all four, but this guidance is architectural inference, not independently sourced this round.

# Digest: routing & dependency injection — round 1

## Q1 — Routing package

**Pick: `go_router`. Fit notes: go_router's `redirect` callback + `refreshListenable` (wrapping the auth Bloc's stream via a `StreamListenable`/ChangeNotifier adapter) is the documented pattern for "redirect to login on session expiry," evaluated globally at the GoRouter level — well-trodden in Flutter/Bloc tutorials. 1	# Verification
2	
3	The trust layer — the same rules whatever produced the material (a native run's digests or a processed import). Verification happens **as material lands**, per dimension, in fresh-context verifier subagents reading digest files — never as an end-of-run rewrite pass over an hour of accumulated context. Late-pass rewrites degrade reports; landing-time checks improve them.
4	
5	## The claims ledger
6	
7	The memlog `claim` entries are the ledger: every claim a decision could rest on, with its class (each pack names its classes — quantitative sizes, pricing, versions/compatibility, regulatory assertions, …), source, publisher, publication date, and status. New claims enter `unverified`; on a Refresh or Deepen run, claims outside the run's scope keep their prior status from the memlog — only new and in-scope claims are (re)checked.
8	
9	## Levels
10	
11	Per the resolved `validation` level (request > knob > default `normal`):
12	
13	- **normal** — spot-check the **load-bearing claims only**: the handful per dimension the recommendation actually rests on. One independent-source check each, at landing. Everything else ships with its single source cited and confidence marked honestly. Fast by design.
14	- **high** — cross-check every claim in the pack's *two-source classes*, and run the red-team pass on major conclusions regardless of `{workflow.red_team}`.
15	- **max** — cross-check every ledger claim, run the red-team pass below at full breadth (every major conclusion), and primary-source-priority ranking: where a primary source (filing, regulator text, official docs, original paper) exists, secondary reporting alone does not verify.
16	
17	Verifier assistants run behind the research firewall on `{workflow.subagent_models}` when set; judgment work never drops to the smallest tier.
18	
19	**Independent** means a different publisher with different underlying data or reporting — not a syndication, quote, or republication of the first source, and not the same vendor's marketing in two places. An imported report counts as one publisher regardless of how many sources it cites internally; two imports from different tools agreeing is genuine confirmation, and their disagreement is a finding.
20	
21	Outcomes per claim: **verified** (independent source agrees within tolerance — for quantitative claims, same order of magnitude and direction), **disputed** (independent sources materially disagree — report both figures, both cited; never average), **unverified** (no independent check within budget — the claim stays, flagged, and joins the staleness map), or **overturned** (the weight of evidence contradicts it — corrected in the text, original noted). Every status change lands in the memlog as a fresh `claim` line with the same `ref=` and the new status — last status wins, which is how `scripts/recon_kit.py tally` reads the ledger. A verification outcome adjusts status and flags — it never licenses rewriting a finding's substance beyond what the new evidence says.
22	
23	Confidence rendered in the report: **high** (verified, fresh, credible publishers), **medium** (single credible source, fresh), **low** (stale, weak publisher, or disputed) — plus the explicit `unverified` flag. Confidence is per-claim, never per-section.
24	
25	## Red-team pass
26	
27	The single adversarial mechanism — no other verifier duplicates it. Off by default (`{workflow.red_team}` = `"off"`; `"offer"` proposes it at the plan gate, `"on"` always runs; `high` validation includes it for major conclusions, `max` runs it at full breadth). When it runs: for each major conclusion, a **fresh-context** skeptic subagent — the conclusion and a search budget, no supporting evidence, no run context — hunts for disconfirming evidence: the bear case, failed attempts, contrary data, the strongest good-faith argument the conclusion is wrong.
28	
29	What comes back is weighed, not appended: a conclusion that survives gets its strongest counter-argument acknowledged in the synthesis; one that doesn't is revised before the report states it. Material findings land in a **Contrary Evidence** section with full citation discipline. Zero findings after a real search is itself reportable — say what was searched for and not found.
30

Confidence rendered in the report: **high** (verified, fresh, credible publishers), **medium** (single credible source, fresh), **low** (stale, weak publisher, or disputed) — plus the explicit `unverified` flag. Confidence is per-claim, never per-section.

## Red-team pass

The single adversarial mechanism — no other verifier duplicates it. Off by default (`{workflow.red_team}` = `"off"`; `"offer"` proposes it at the plan gate, `"on"` always runs; `high` validation includes it for major conclusions, `max` runs it at full breadth). When it runs: for each major conclusion, a **fresh-context** skeptic subagent — the conclusion and a search budget, no supporting evidence, no run context — hunts for disconfirming evidence: the bear case, failed attempts, contrary data, the strongest good-faith argument the conclusion is wrong.

What comes back is weighed, not appended: a conclusion that survives gets its strongest counter-argument acknowledged in the synthesis; one that doesn't is revised before the report states it. Material findings land in a **Contrary Evidence** section with full citation discipline. Zero findings after a real search is itself reportable — say what was searched for and not found.

title: 'technical research: Flutter package selection for F000 and RF03 free-choice slots'
type: 'technical'
topic: 'Flutter package selection for F000 and RF03 free-choice slots'
decision: 'Pick concrete packages for Cerne''s six free-choice technical slots (routing, HTTP client, local cache, dependency injection, secure storage, biometrics), needed for F000 (foundation) and RF03 (biometric vault), the next two units in the delivery order.'
source: 'run'
status: complete
preset: 'standard'
validation: 'normal'

---

# technical research: Flutter package selection for F000 and RF03 free-choice slots

**Decision this research serves:** Pick concrete packages for Cerne's six free-choice technical slots (routing, HTTP client, local cache, dependency injection, secure storage, biometrics), needed for F000 (foundation) and RF03 (biometric vault), the next two units in the delivery order.

## Executive summary

Six picks, each with a clear runner-up and switch condition:

| Slot | Pick | Runner-up | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Routing | `go_router` | `auto_route` | High |
| HTTP client | `dio` | `package:http` | High |
| Local cache / persistence | `drift` | `sqflite` | High |
| Dependency injection | `get_it` | `riverpod`-as-DI | Medium-high |
| Secure storage | `flutter_secure_storage` | `flutter_keychain` | High |
| Biometrics | `local_auth` | none (sole credible candidate) | High |

The driving pattern across all six: **avoid build-time codegen unless it earns its keep.** `go_router`, `get_it`, and `dio` all have codegen-based siblings (`auto_route`+generator, `injectable`, `chopper`) that are credible but add a `build_runner` step a solo developer on a fixed timeline doesn't need yet — every codegen alternative is kept as the documented upgrade path, not dismissed. The other driving pattern: **two of the "obvious" NoSQL picks are traps.** Both `isar` and `hive`, the packages most tutorials still point to, have their original packages effectively abandoned (last releases 2022–2023); only community forks remain. `drift` (SQLite, actively maintained, Flutter Favorite) avoids that risk entirely.

Biggest caveat: none of these picks were checked against each other for cross-package friction (e.g., `dio` + `flutter_secure_storage` + `get_it` wired together) — each was researched independently. This is a reasonable risk to accept (all six are mainstream, independently popular, non-exotic choices with no known incompatibilities surfaced), but it is an open question, not a verified fact.

## 1. Routing

**Pick: `go_router`. Runner-up: `auto_route`.**

| Criterion | `go_router` | `auto_route` | `Beamer` | GetX router |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Fit: `flutter_bloc` redirect-on-session-expiry | Documented pattern via `redirect` + `refreshListenable` [30] | Supported, less first-party-documented | Not screened | Poor prior fit, not screened |
| Clean Architecture fit | Pure presentation layer, no codegen required [1][26] | Pure presentation layer, needs `build_runner` + annotations | — | — |
| Maturity / adoption | Flutter-team-maintained, larger adoption, 4,435 likes [1][26][27] | Active (11.1.0, Dec 2025; generator 10.5.0, Feb 2026), 3.39K likes, smaller ecosystem [5][28] | Last GitHub push reported Oct 2024, no 2025/2026 activity found [29] | Not researched |
| Learning curve (solo dev, deadline) | No codegen, largest tutorial volume | One more moving part (codegen) | — | — |
| Cut reason | — | Kept as runner-up | Stale — screened out | Conflicts with `flutter_bloc` + Clean Architecture commitments; not pursued |

**Switch condition:** move to `auto_route` if compile-time-checked route arguments become worth a second codegen pipeline, or if `go_router`'s maintenance-mode status (Flutter team shipping bug fixes, not new features [27]) turns into an actually-missing capability.

**Verified at landing:** the "go_router is still the right 2026 default" verdict was single-sourced to a Feb 2025 article [27]; an independent, fresher check (Jul 2026) reached the same conclusion [36] — **status: verified**. A separate claim in [27] that `auto_route` was "stagnating" is **overturned** by current `auto_route` release data showing active Dec 2025/Feb 2026 releases [5][28] — `auto_route` is not stagnant, it is simply smaller.

**Unverified pain-point (flagged, not a finding):** reports of `go_router` API instability across versions and `StatefulShellRoute` complaints surfaced only as a single aggregated search synthesis [31], not two independent primary sources. Treat as a signal worth watching during implementation, not a confirmed flaw.

## 2. HTTP client

**Pick: `dio`. Runner-up: `package:http`.**

| Criterion | `dio` | `package:http` | `chopper` |
|---|---|---|---|
| Header injection (apikey always, Bearer conditionally) | First-class `Interceptor`s, global + per-request [1] | No built-in interceptor system — needs hand-extending `BaseClient.send()` or a third-party add-on [7][8] | Interceptor support exists but gated behind codegen |
| Retry on `retryable:true` error codes | Documented `retryEvaluator` pattern keyed off exception type/status [2][3] | Manual | Not independently checked |
| Mapping into `Either<Failure,T>` | Single typed `DioException` on every failure path — narrow, clean catch surface [1] | Throws various exception types; no unifying type | Not independently checked |
| Testability (`mocktail`) | `MockDio` or `http_mock_adapter` [4][5] | Mockable, simpler surface | Not independently checked |
| Maturity | 160 pub points, 8.37k likes, 5.2M weekly downloads [1] | First-party Dart-team package | 906 likes, needs `build_runner` [6] |

**Switch condition:** only to `chopper`, only if the project later wants Retrofit-style typed API clients and accepts a `build_runner` pipeline — not recommended given the timeline.

## 3. Local cache / persistence

**Pick: `drift`. Runner-up: `sqflite`.**

| Criterion | `drift` | `sqflite` | `isar` | `hive` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Maintenance status | Actively published (~2 days old at check), Flutter Favorite, verified publisher [20] | Flutter Favorite, no codegen [21] | **Original package abandoned** — last release Apr 2023; only `isar_community` fork remains [15][16] | **Original packages abandoned** — last releases 2021/2022; only `hive_ce` fork remains [17][18][19] |
| Fit: filter by sync status (`pending`/`synced`/`failed`) | Native SQL `WHERE` filtering | Native SQL `WHERE` filtering, hand-written | Possible via fork, less direct | Possible via fork, less direct |
| Codegen cost | `build_runner` required | None — hand-written SQL/mapping | Fork-dependent | Fork-dependent |
| Risk | Low — primary package itself is healthy | Low — but hand-rolled mapping | **Elevated** — fork-maintenance risk, smaller/younger community | **Elevated** — same fork risk |

**Switch condition:** drop to `sqflite` if `build_runner`/codegen friction becomes a real blocker on a solo timeline — the schema here (an entries table + a `syncStatus` column) is simple enough that losing codegen costs little.

# technical research: Flutter package selection for F000 and RF03 free-choice slots

| Local cache / persistence | `drift` | `sqflite` | High |
| Dependency injection | `get_it` | `riverpod`-as-DI | Medium-high |
| Secure storage | `flutter_secure_storage` | `flutter_keychain` | High |
| Biometrics | `local_auth` | none (sole credible candidate) | High |

Biggest caveat: none of these picks were checked against each other for cross-package friction (e.g., `dio` + `flutter_secure_storage` + `get_it` wired together) — each was researched independently. # technical research: Flutter package selection for F000 and RF03 free-choice slots

**Decision this research serves:** Pick concrete packages for Cerne's six free-choice technical slots (routing, HTTP client, local cache, dependency injection, secure storage, biometrics), needed for F000 (foundation) and RF03 (biometric vault), the next two units in the delivery order.

## Executive summary

Six picks, each with a clear runner-up and switch condition:

| Slot | Pick | Runner-up | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Routing | `go_router` | `auto_route` | High |
| HTTP client | `dio` | `package:http` | High |
| Local cache / persistence | `drift` | `sqflite` | High |
| Dependency injection | `get_it` | `riverpod`-as-DI | Medium-high |
| Secure storage | `flutter_secure_storage` | `flutter_keychain` | High |
| Biometrics | `local_auth` | none (sole credible candidate) | High |

The driving pattern across all six: **avoid build-time codegen unless it earns its keep.** `go_router`, `get_it`, and `dio` all have codegen-based siblings (`auto_route`+generator, `injectable`, `chopper`) that are credible but add a `build_runner` step a solo developer on a fixed timeline doesn't need yet — every codegen alternative is kept as the documented upgrade path, not dismissed. The other driving pattern: **two of the "obvious" NoSQL picks are traps.** Both `isar` and `hive`, the packages most tutorials still point to, have their original packages effectively abandoned (last releases 2022–2023); only community forks remain. `drift` (SQLite, actively maintained, Flutter Favorite) avoids that risk entirely.

Biggest caveat: none of these picks were checked against each other for cross-package friction (e.g., `dio` + `flutter_secure_storage` + `get_it` wired together) — each was researched independently. This is a reasonable risk to accept (all six are mainstream, independently popular, non-exotic choices with no known incompatibilities surfaced), but it is an open question, not a verified fact.

## 1. Routing

**Pick: `go_router`. Runner-up: `auto_route`.**

| Criterion | `go_router` | `auto_route` | `Beamer` | GetX router |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Fit: `flutter_bloc` redirect-on-session-expiry | Documented pattern via `redirect` + `refreshListenable` [30] | Supported, less first-party-documented | Not screened | Poor prior fit, not screened |
| Clean Architecture fit | Pure presentation layer, no codegen required [1][26] | Pure presentation layer, needs `build_runner` + annotations | — | — |
| Maturity / adoption | Flutter-team-maintained, larger adoption, 4,435 likes [1][26][27] | Active (11.1.0, Dec 2025; generator 10.5.0, Feb 2026), 3.39K likes, smaller ecosystem [5][28] | Last GitHub push reported Oct 2024, no 2025/2026 activity found [29] | Not researched |
| Learning curve (solo dev, deadline) | No codegen, largest tutorial volume | One more moving part (codegen) | — | — |
| Cut reason | — | Kept as runner-up | Stale — screened out | Conflicts with `flutter_bloc` + Clean Architecture commitments; not pursued |

**Switch condition:** move to `auto_route` if compile-time-checked route arguments become worth a second codegen pipeline, or if `go_router`'s maintenance-mode status (Flutter team shipping bug fixes, not new features [27]) turns into an actually-missing capability.

**Verified at landing:** the "go_router is still the right 2026 default" verdict was single-sourced to a Feb 2025 article [27]; an independent, fresher check (Jul 2026) reached the same conclusion [36] — **status: verified**. A separate claim in [27] that `auto_route` was "stagnating" is **overturned** by current `auto_route` release data showing active Dec 2025/Feb 2026 releases [5][28] — `auto_route` is not stagnant, it is simply smaller.

**Unverified pain-point (flagged, not a finding):** reports of `go_router` API instability across versions and `StatefulShellRoute` complaints surfaced only as a single aggregated search synthesis [31], not two independent primary sources. Treat as a signal worth watching during implementation, not a confirmed flaw.

## 2. HTTP client

**Pick: `dio`. Runner-up: `package:http`.**

| Criterion | `dio` | `package:http` | `chopper` |
|---|---|---|---|
| Header injection (apikey always, Bearer conditionally) | First-class `Interceptor`s, global + per-request [1] | No built-in interceptor system — needs hand-extending `BaseClient.send()` or a third-party add-on [7][8] | Interceptor support exists but gated behind codegen |
| Retry on `retryable:true` error codes | Documented `retryEvaluator` pattern keyed off exception type/status [2][3] | Manual | Not independently checked |
| Mapping into `Either<Failure,T>` | Single typed `DioException` on every failure path — narrow, clean catch surface [1] | Throws various exception types; no unifying type | Not independently checked |
| Testability (`mocktail`) | `MockDio` or `http_mock_adapter` [4][5] | Mockable, simpler surface | Not independently checked |
| Maturity | 160 pub points, 8.37k likes, 5.2M weekly downloads [1] | First-party Dart-team package | 906 likes, needs `build_runner` [6] |

**Switch condition:** only to `chopper`, only if the project later wants Retrofit-style typed API clients and accepts a `build_runner` pipeline — not recommended given the timeline.

## 3. Local cache / persistence

**Pick: `drift`. Runner-up: `sqflite`.**

| Criterion | `drift` | `sqflite` | `isar` | `hive` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Maintenance status | Actively published (~2 days old at check), Flutter Favorite, verified publisher [20] | Flutter Favorite, no codegen [21] | **Original package abandoned** — last release Apr 2023; only `isar_community` fork remains [15][16] | **Original packages abandoned** — last releases 2021/2022; only `hive_ce` fork remains [17][18][19] |
| Fit: filter by sync status (`pending`/`synced`/`failed`) | Native SQL `WHERE` filtering | Native SQL `WHERE` filtering, hand-written | Possible via fork, less direct | Possible via fork, less direct |
| Codegen cost | `build_runner` required | None — hand-written SQL/mapping | Fork-dependent | Fork-dependent |
| Risk | Low — primary package itself is healthy | Low — but hand-rolled mapping | **Elevated** — fork-maintenance risk, smaller/younger community | **Elevated** — same fork risk |

**Switch condition:** drop to `sqflite` if `build_runner`/codegen friction becomes a real blocker on a solo timeline — the schema here (an entries table + a `syncStatus` column) is simple enough that losing codegen costs little.

**Note (not independently sourced, architectural inference):** none of the four candidates expose `Either` natively — all throw exceptions, so the repository layer catches and maps to `Failure` regardless of pick. Not a differentiator between candidates.

## 4. Dependency injection

**Pick: `get_it`** (manual registration at a single composition root; skip `injectable` unless registration volume gets painful). **Runner-up: `riverpod`-as-DI.**

| Criterion | `get_it` | `riverpod`-as-DI | `injectable` (codegen add-on) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Flutter-free (RNF06 — domain never imports `flutter`) | Pure Dart, no Flutter dependency [32] | Non-Flutter core package, usable without Flutter dependency | N/A — add-on to `get_it` |
| Testability | Singleton locator, but explicitly designed to reset/override per test (`getIt.reset()`, `pushNewScope()`) — satisfies "no untestable hidden singleton" in practice, though it architecturally *is* a singleton | Provider-override (`overrideWithValue`) arguably cleaner for test swapping | Same as `get_it` |
| Fit alongside `flutter_bloc` | Standard: `BlocProvider(create: (_) => getIt<MyBloc>())` | No current production source found pairing Riverpod-as-DI underneath `flutter_bloc` — unverified/thin combination | — |
| Maturity | 140/140 pub points, 4.7K likes, 1.7M downloads/30d [32] | Not independently checked as standalone signal | v3.0.0, LeanBuilder since 2.12.0+ fixes historical slow-build complaint [33] |

**Switch condition:** only if the project drops `flutter_bloc` for Riverpod's own state-management primitives — running two separate reactive/DI paradigms side by side adds avoidable conceptual overhead on a solo deadline.

**Explicit gap:** `provider` and "no-package manual DI" were named candidates but not researched this round — no claims are reported for them; they are not evidenced as cut, simply not pursued.

## 5. Secure storage

**Pick: `flutter_secure_storage`. Runner-up: `flutter_keychain`.**

| Criterion | `flutter_secure_storage` | `flutter_keychain` |
|---|---|---|
| Maintenance | 160 pub points, 4.5k likes, 5.64M weekly downloads, last published ~39 days before check, verified publisher [9] | Latest 3.0.1 (~Mar 2026), far smaller footprint — "small and quiet," not confirmed "small and solid" [14, unverified] |
| iOS Keychain control | Exposes `IOSOptions(accessibility: ...)` directly, including `first_unlock`/`first_unlock_this_device` [11][12] — the control needed for "readable after biometric unlock, survives restart" | Not independently checked |
| Known pitfall | v10→v11 breaking change (custom cipher); pre-v10 data needs the v10 migration step before jumping to v11 or becomes unreadable [9][10] | — |
| Testability | Trivially abstracted behind a repository interface, mockable | Same |

**Switch condition:** none realistic for an iOS-only app — would only apply if the v10/v11 migration caused unresolvable data loss, or Android-specific tuning were needed (it isn't).

**Architectural note, not independently sourced:** Keychain accessibility classes govern *device*-lock state, not the app's own biometric re-auth gate — RF03's 5-minute-timeout re-auth logic sits on top of, not inside, whichever storage package is chosen.

**Unverified pain-point:** reported iOS Keychain error codes (-25308, -25291) around app restart/background are single-source/anecdotal [13] — no second source found; not treated as a confirmed, current issue.

## 6. Biometrics

**Pick: `local_auth`. No real runner-up — sole credible candidate.**

A hand-rolled platform-channel implementation was considered and rejected: it duplicates what the plugin already does, with no documented upside found for a solo-dev timeline.

- Maturity: verified `flutter.dev` publisher, 160 pub points, 3.38k likes, 1.82M weekly downloads, last release ~3 months before check [22].
- `NSFaceIDUsageDescription` is required in `Info.plist` for Face ID; not required for Touch ID [23].
- `AuthenticationOptions.stickyAuth`: `true` resumes an in-flight auth when the app returns to foreground; `false` (default) returns immediate failure on backgrounding — the app decides whether to restart it [24]. The 5-minute idle-timeout gate itself (RF03) is app-level logic built on `WidgetsBindingObserver`/`didChangeAppLifecycleState`, not something the plugin provides.
- Biometric lockout (`LAError.biometryLockout`/`lockedOut`) after repeated failures can only be cleared by the user entering the device passcode — no programmatic reset. The app must catch this and route to a passcode-entry fallback rather than retry biometrics [23][25].

**Switch condition:** none identified — only if `local_auth` became unmaintained, which current data does not support.

## Cross-dimension insights

- **The codegen-avoidance pattern recurs independently three times** (routing vs. `auto_route`, DI vs. `injectable`, HTTP vs. `chopper`) — each dimension was researched in isolation, yet all three landed on "skip the codegen sibling for now, keep it as a named upgrade path." That consistency is itself a weak signal that the "no codegen yet" call is the right default for this project's size and timeline, not an artifact of one researcher's bias.
- **The abandoned-package trap is specific to the local-cache dimension.** No other category had a "popular package, but actually dead" result — `isar`/`hive` is a real, non-obvious risk this research caught; a developer going by package-name familiarity alone (both are still widely referenced in older tutorials) would have picked a fork-dependent, higher-risk option without knowing it.
- **Biometrics and secure storage are adjacent but distinct concerns that a less careful pick could conflate.** `local_auth` gates *access*; `flutter_secure_storage`'s Keychain accessibility class governs *when stored data is readable relative to device-lock state* — the RF03 "5-minute background timeout → re-auth" flow needs both, wired together at the app layer, and neither package solves the other's half.

## Open questions

- **Cross-package integration friction** (e.g., `dio` + `flutter_secure_storage` + `get_it` wired together in the same composition root) was not tested — each pick was researched independently. Resolving this needs hands-on integration during F000, not more research.
- **`go_router`'s version-to-version API stability** complaint [31] is a single aggregated, unattributed synthesis — resolving it needs a direct read of `github.com/flutter/packages` issues filtered for `go_router` + "breaking change."

- **`provider` and manual-constructor DI** (named Q2 candidates) and **GetX's router** (named Q1 candidate) were never researched — if either is later reconsidered, this report provides no evidence on them either way.
- **`riverpod`-as-DI-under-`flutter_bloc`** is a named runner-up with no current production source evidencing the combination works well in practice — treat it as a reasoned inference, not a verified pattern, if ever promoted from runner-up to pick.

**Decision this research serves:** Pick concrete packages for Cerne's six free-choice technical slots (routing, HTTP client, local cache, dependency injection, secure storage, biometrics), needed for F000 (foundation) and RF03 (biometric vault), the next two units in the delivery order.
-_Sections are appended per the approved research plan; the executive summary is written last and placed here, first._
+## Executive summary
+Six picks, each with a clear runner-up and switch condition:
+| Slot | Pick | Runner-up | Confidence |
+| Routing | `go_router` | `auto_route` | High |
+| HTTP client | `dio` | `package:http` | High |
+| Local cache / persistence | `drift` | `sqflite` | High |
+| Dependency injection | `get_it` | `riverpod`-as-DI | Medium-high |
+| Secure storage | `flutter_secure_storage` | `flutter_keychain` | High |
+| Biometrics | `local_auth` | none (sole credible candidate) | High |

+The driving pattern across all six: **avoid build-time codegen unless it earns its keep.** `go_router`, `get_it`, and `dio` all have codegen-based siblings (`auto_route`+generator, `injectable`, `chopper`) that are credible but add a `build_runner` step a solo developer on a fixed timeline doesn't need yet — every codegen alternative is kept as the documented upgrade path, not dismissed. The other driving pattern: **two of the "obvious" NoSQL picks are traps.** Both `isar` and `hive`, the packages most tutorials still point to, have their original packages effectively abandoned (last releases 2022–2023); only community forks remain. `drift` (SQLite, actively maintained, Flutter Favorite) avoids that risk entirely.

+Biggest caveat: none of these picks were checked against each other for cross-package friction (e.g., `dio` + `flutter_secure_storage` + `get_it` wired together) — each was researched independently. This is a reasonable risk to accept (all six are mainstream, independently popular, non-exotic choices with no known incompatibilities surfaced), but it is an open question, not a verified fact.
+## 1. Routing
+**Pick: `go_router`. Runner-up: `auto_route`.**
+| Criterion | `go_router` | `auto_route` | `Beamer` | GetX router |

+| Fit: `flutter_bloc` redirect-on-session-expiry | Documented pattern via `redirect` + `refreshListenable` [30] | Supported, less first-party-documented | Not screened | Poor prior fit, not screened |
+| Clean Architecture fit | Pure presentation layer, no codegen required [1][26] | Pure presentation layer, needs `build_runner` + annotations | — | — |

+| Maturity / adoption | Flutter-team-maintained, larger adoption, 4,435 likes [1][26][27] | Active (11.1.0, Dec 2025; generator 10.5.0, Feb 2026), 3.39K likes, smaller ecosystem [5][28] | Last GitHub push reported Oct 2024, no 2025/2026 activity found [29] | Not researched |
+| Learning curve (solo dev, deadline) | No codegen, largest tutorial volume | One more moving part (codegen) | — | — |
+| Cut reason | — | Kept as runner-up | Stale — screened out | Conflicts with `flutter_bloc` + Clean Architecture commitments; not pursued |

+**Switch condition:** move to `auto_route` if compile-time-checked route arguments become worth a second codegen pipeline, or if `go_router`'s maintenance-mode status (Flutter team shipping bug fixes, not new features [27]) turns into an actually-missing capability.

+**Verified at landing:** the "go_router is still the right 2026 default" verdict was single-sourced to a Feb 2025 article [27]; an independent, fresher check (Jul 2026) reached the same conclusion [36] — **status: verified**. A separate claim in [27] that `auto_route` was "stagnating" is **overturned** by current `auto_route` release data showing active Dec 2025/Feb 2026 releases [5][28] — `auto_route` is not stagnant, it is simply smaller.

+**Unverified pain-point (flagged, not a finding):** reports of `go_router` API instability across versions and `StatefulShellRoute` complaints surfaced only as a single aggregated search synthesis [31], not two independent primary sources. Treat as a signal worth watching during implementation, not a confirmed flaw.
+## 2. HTTP client
+**Pick: `dio`. Runner-up: `package:http`.**
+| Criterion | `dio` | `package:http` | `chopper` |

+| Header injection (apikey always, Bearer conditionally) | First-class `Interceptor`s, global + per-request [1] | No built-in interceptor system — needs hand-extending `BaseClient.send()` or a third-party add-on [7][8] | Interceptor support exists but gated behind codegen |
+| Retry on `retryable:true` error codes | Documented `retryEvaluator` pattern keyed off exception type/status [2][3] | Manual | Not independently checked |

+| Mapping into `Either<Failure,T>` | Single typed `DioException` on every failure path — narrow, clean catch surface [1] | Throws various exception types; no unifying type | Not independently checked |
+| Testability (`mocktail`) | `MockDio` or `http_mock_adapter` [4][5] | Mockable, simpler surface | Not independently checked |
+| Maturity | 160 pub points, 8.37k likes, 5.2M weekly downloads [1] | First-party Dart-team package | 906 likes, needs `build_runner` [6] |
+**Switch condition:** only to `chopper`, only if the project later wants Retrofit-style typed API clients and accepts a `build_runner` pipeline — not recommended given the timeline.
+## 3. Local cache / persistence
+**Pick: `drift`. Runner-up: `sqflite`.**
+| Criterion | `drift` | `sqflite` | `isar` | `hive` |

+| Maintenance status | Actively published (~2 days old at check), Flutter Favorite, verified publisher [20] | Flutter Favorite, no codegen [21] | **Original package abandoned** — last release Apr 2023; only `isar_community` fork remains [15][16] | **Original packages abandoned** — last releases 2021/2022; only `hive_ce` fork remains [17][18][19] |

+| Fit: filter by sync status (`pending`/`synced`/`failed`) | Native SQL `WHERE` filtering | Native SQL `WHERE` filtering, hand-written | Possible via fork, less direct | Possible via fork, less direct |
+| Codegen cost | `build_runner` required | None — hand-written SQL/mapping | Fork-dependent | Fork-dependent |
+| Risk | Low — primary package itself is healthy | Low — but hand-rolled mapping | **Elevated** — fork-maintenance risk, smaller/younger community | **Elevated** — same fork risk |

+**Switch condition:** drop to `sqflite` if `build_runner`/codegen friction becomes a real blocker on a solo timeline — the schema here (an entries table + a `syncStatus` column) is simple enough that losing codegen costs little.

+**Note (not independently sourced, architectural inference):** none of the four candidates expose `Either` natively — all throw exceptions, so the repository layer catches and maps to `Failure` regardless of pick. Not a differentiator between candidates.
+## 4. Dependency injection
+**Pick: `get_it`** (manual registration at a single composition root; skip `injectable` unless registration volume gets painful). **Runner-up: `riverpod`-as-DI.**
+| Criterion | `get_it` | `riverpod`-as-DI | `injectable` (codegen add-on) |
+| Flutter-free (RNF06 — domain never imports `flutter`) | Pure Dart, no Flutter dependency [32] | Non-Flutter core package, usable without Flutter dependency | N/A — add-on to `get_it` |

+| Testability | Singleton locator, but explicitly designed to reset/override per test (`getIt.reset()`, `pushNewScope()`) — satisfies "no untestable hidden singleton" in practice, though it architecturally *is* a singleton | Provider-override (`overrideWithValue`) arguably cleaner for test swapping | Same as `get_it` |

+| Fit alongside `flutter_bloc` | Standard: `BlocProvider(create: (_) => getIt<MyBloc>())` | No current production source found pairing Riverpod-as-DI underneath `flutter_bloc` — unverified/thin combination | — |
+| Maturity | 140/140 pub points, 4.7K likes, 1.7M downloads/30d [32] | Not independently checked as standalone signal | v3.0.0, LeanBuilder since 2.12.0+ fixes historical slow-build complaint [33] |

+**Switch condition:** only if the project drops `flutter_bloc` for Riverpod's own state-management primitives — running two separate reactive/DI paradigms side by side adds avoidable conceptual overhead on a solo deadline.
+**Explicit gap:** `provider` and "no-package manual DI" were named candidates but not researched this round — no claims are reported for them; they are not evidenced as cut, simply not pursued.
+## 5. Secure storage
+**Pick: `flutter_secure_storage`. Runner-up: `flutter_keychain`.**
+| Criterion | `flutter_secure_storage` | `flutter_keychain` |

+| Maintenance | 160 pub points, 4.5k likes, 5.64M weekly downloads, last published ~39 days before check, verified publisher [9] | Latest 3.0.1 (~Mar 2026), far smaller footprint — "small and quiet," not confirmed "small and solid" [14, unverified] |

+| iOS Keychain control | Exposes `IOSOptions(accessibility: ...)` directly, including `first_unlock`/`first_unlock_this_device` [11][12] — the control needed for "readable after biometric unlock, survives restart" | Not independently checked |
+| Known pitfall | v10→v11 breaking change (custom cipher); pre-v10 data needs the v10 migration step before jumping to v11 or becomes unreadable [9][10] | — |
+| Testability | Trivially abstracted behind a repository interface, mockable | Same |
+**Switch condition:** none realistic for an iOS-only app — would only apply if the v10/v11 migration caused unresolvable data loss, or Android-specific tuning were needed (it isn't).

+**Architectural note, not independently sourced:** Keychain accessibility classes govern *device*-lock state, not the app's own biometric re-auth gate — RF03's 5-minute-timeout re-auth logic sits on top of, not inside, whichever storage package is chosen.

+**Unverified pain-point:** reported iOS Keychain error codes (-25308, -25291) around app restart/background are single-source/anecdotal [13] — no second source found; not treated as a confirmed, current issue.
+## 6. Biometrics
+**Pick: `local_auth`. No real runner-up — sole credible candidate.**
+A hand-rolled platform-channel implementation was considered and rejected: it duplicates what the plugin already does, with no documented upside found for a solo-dev timeline.
+- Maturity: verified `flutter.dev` publisher, 160 pub points, 3.38k likes, 1.82M weekly downloads, last release ~3 months before check [22].
+- `NSFaceIDUsageDescription` is required in `Info.plist` for Face ID; not required for Touch ID [23].

+- `AuthenticationOptions.stickyAuth`: `true` resumes an in-flight auth when the app returns to foreground; `false` (default) returns immediate failure on backgrounding — the app decides whether to restart it [24]. The 5-minute idle-timeout gate itself (RF03) is app-level logic built on `WidgetsBindingObserver`/`didChangeAppLifecycleState`, not something the plugin provides.

+- Biometric lockout (`LAError.biometryLockout`/`lockedOut`) after repeated failures can only be cleared by the user entering the device passcode — no programmatic reset. The app must catch this and route to a passcode-entry fallback rather than retry biometrics [23][25].
+**Switch condition:** none identified — only if `local_auth` became unmaintained, which current data does not support.
+## Cross-dimension insights

+- **The codegen-avoidance pattern recurs independently three times** (routing vs. `auto_route`, DI vs. `injectable`, HTTP vs. `chopper`) — each dimension was researched in isolation, yet all three landed on "skip the codegen sibling for now, keep it as a named upgrade path." That consistency is itself a weak signal that the "no codegen yet" call is the right default for this project's size and timeline, not an artifact of one researcher's bias.

+- **The abandoned-package trap is specific to the local-cache dimension.** No other category had a "popular package, but actually dead" result — `isar`/`hive` is a real, non-obvious risk this research caught; a developer going by package-name familiarity alone (both are still widely referenced in older tutorials) would have picked a fork-dependent, higher-risk option without knowing it.

+- **Biometrics and secure storage are adjacent but distinct concerns that a less careful pick could conflate.** `local_auth` gates *access*; `flutter_secure_storage`'s Keychain accessibility class governs *when stored data is readable relative to device-lock state* — the RF03 "5-minute background timeout → re-auth" flow needs both, wired together at the app layer, and neither package solves the other's half.
+## Open questions

+- **Cross-package integration friction** (e.g., `dio` + `flutter_secure_storage` + `get_it` wired together in the same composition root) was not tested — each pick was researched independently. Resolving this needs hands-on integration during F000, not more research.

+- **`go_router`'s version-to-version API stability** complaint [31] is a single aggregated, unattributed synthesis — resolving it needs a direct read of `github.com/flutter/packages` issues filtered for `go_router` + "breaking change."

+- **`flutter_secure_storage`'s iOS Keychain error codes (-25308/-25291) on restart/background** [13] — resolving it needs a direct search of `github.com/juliansteenbakker/flutter_secure_storage/issues` filtered for "iOS" + "restart"; currently single-source/anecdotal.

+- **`provider` and manual-constructor DI** (named Q2 candidates) and **GetX's router** (named Q1 candidate) were never researched — if either is later reconsidered, this report provides no evidence on them either way.

+- **`riverpod`-as-DI-under-`flutter_bloc`** is a named runner-up with no current production source evidencing the combination works well in practice — treat it as a reasoned inference, not a verified pattern, if ever promoted from runner-up to pick.

# HTML Briefing

Generate `research-briefing.html` in `{doc_workspace}` after `research.md` is final, when `{workflow.output_format}` calls for it: `"auto"` renders on interactive runs and skips on headless/skill-invoked runs (the md is always there to render from later), `"html"`/`"both"` always render, `"md"` never. The page is a full-fidelity presentation of the report, never a second source of truth — same claims, same numbers, same citations; nothing is lost by reading it instead of the markdown.

## Requirements

- **Self-contained single file**: inline CSS and JS, no external requests of any kind (no CDN, no fonts, no remote images). It must render from a `file://` open, offline, forever.
- **Structure**: a header (topic, type, decision, date, depth, verification level) → the executive summary as the opening card → sticky table of contents → dimension sections → contrary evidence (when present) → recommendations → collapsible source appendix → staleness map.
- **Confidence is visual**: every claim carries its badge — verified / medium / low / `unverified` / disputed — color-coded with the status text always present (never color alone). Unverified and disputed must be *more* prominent than verified, not less.
- **Sources are live**: inline `[n]` markers link to the appendix row; appendix rows link out to the source URL. Source URLs are untrusted content — never hand-escape them: generate the appendix table with `uv run scripts/recon_kit.py escape-sources {doc_workspace}/research.md` and embed its `html` output, which escapes every cell, anchors each row (`id="src-n"`), and links only validated `http(s)` URLs (anything else renders as plain text; the script lists it in `invalid_urls`). Apply the same escape discipline to any other source-derived text you place in attributes.
- **Charts sparingly**: only where the data genuinely benefits (market size trajectory, decision matrix scores) — simple inline SVG, labeled axes, no library.
- **Responsive and theme-aware**: readable on a phone; respect `prefers-color-scheme` for light/dark.

## Theme

`{workflow.html_theme}` governs: a `file:` path loads a theme/brand spec to follow; inline text is applied as directives; empty means the shipped default — neutral, professional, generous whitespace, system font stack, one restrained accent color. Whatever the theme, the confidence-badge semantics above are non-negotiable.

Flutter package selection — F000 / RF03 free-choice slots

Type: technical research (select shape) Date: 2026-10-25 Depth: standard preset, 1 round, 3 parallel assistants Verification: normal — load-bearing spot-check, semantic citation check applied
Decision this research serves: pick concrete packages for Cerne's six free-choice technical slots (routing, HTTP client, local cache, dependency injection, secure storage, biometrics) — needed for F000 (foundation) and RF03 (biometric vault), the next two units in the delivery order.
Summary Routing HTTP client Local cache DI Secure storage Biometrics Cross-dimension Open questions Sources Staleness

Executive summary

Routing
go_router
runner-up: auto_route
HTTP client
dio
runner-up: package:http
Local cache
drift
runner-up: sqflite
Dependency injection
get_it
runner-up: riverpod-as-DI
Secure storage
flutter_secure_storage
runner-up: flutter_keychain
Biometrics
local_auth
sole credible candidate

The driving pattern across all six: avoid build-time codegen unless it earns its keep. go_router, get_it, and dio each have codegen-based siblings (auto_route+generator, injectable, chopper) that are credible but add a build_runner step a solo developer on a fixed timeline doesn't need yet — every codegen alternative is kept as a named upgrade path, not dismissed.

Second pattern: two of the "obvious" NoSQL picks are traps. Both isar and hive — the packages most tutorials still point to — have their original packages effectively abandoned (last releases 2022–2023); only community forks remain. drift avoids that risk entirely.

Biggest caveat: no cross-package integration friction was tested (e.g. dio + flutter_secure_storage + get_it wired together) — each pick was researched independently. Reasonable to accept given all six are mainstream, popular choices, but it's an open question, not a verified fact.

1. Routing — go_router

Runner-up: auto_route. Switch if compile-time-checked route arguments become worth a second codegen pipeline, or if go_router's maintenance-mode status becomes an actually-missing capability.
Criteriongo_routerauto_routeBeamer / GetX
Fit: flutter_bloc redirect-on-expiryDocumented redirect + refreshListenable pattern [30]Supported, less first-party-documentedNot screened
Clean Architecture fitPure presentation layer, no codegen [26]Needs build_runner + annotations—
Maturity / adoptionFlutter-team-maintained, 4,435 likes [26][27]Active (Dec 2025/Feb 2026 releases), 3.39K likes [28]Beamer: last push Oct 2024 [29]; GetX: not researched

verified "go_router is still the right 2026 default" — single-sourced to a Feb 2025 article [27], independently re-confirmed by a fresher Jul 2026 source [36].

overturned [27]'s claim that auto_route was "stagnating" — contradicted by current release data [28]; auto_route is smaller, not stagnant.

unverified go_router "API instability across versions" / StatefulShellRoute complaints — single aggregated synthesis [31], not two independent sources.

2. HTTP client — dio

Runner-up: package:http. Switch to chopper only if typed Retrofit-style clients become worth a codegen pipeline — not recommended here.
Criteriondiopackage:httpchopper
Header injection (apikey always, Bearer conditional)First-class Interceptors, global + per-request [1]No built-in interceptors [7][8]Interceptors exist, gated behind codegen
Retry on retryable codesretryEvaluator pattern [2][3]ManualNot checked
Maps to Either<Failure,T>Single typed DioException on every failure [1]Various exception types, no unifying typeNot checked
TestabilityMockDio / http_mock_adapter [4][5]Mockable, simpler surfaceNot checked
Maturity8.37k likes, 5.2M weekly downloads [1]First-party Dart-team package906 likes, needs build_runner [6]

3. Local cache / persistence — drift

Runner-up: sqflite. Switch to sqflite if build_runner friction becomes a real blocker — the schema (entries + a syncStatus column) is simple enough that losing codegen costs little.
Criteriondriftsqfliteisarhive
MaintenanceActively published, Flutter Favorite [20]Flutter Favorite, no codegen [21]Original abandoned (last release Apr 2023) [15][16]Original abandoned (2021/2022) [17][18][19]
RiskLowLow (hand-rolled mapping)Elevated — fork-maintenance riskElevated — fork-maintenance risk

None of the four expose Either natively — all throw exceptions; repository layer maps to Failure regardless of pick. Not a differentiator (architectural inference, not independently sourced).

4. Dependency injection — get_it

Runner-up: riverpod-as-DI. Switch only if the project drops flutter_bloc entirely for Riverpod's own state primitives.
Criterionget_itriverpod-as-DIinjectable (add-on)
Flutter-free (RNF06)Pure Dart, no Flutter dep (architectural inference)Usable without Flutter depN/A
TestabilitySingleton locator, explicitly reset/override-able per testProvider-override arguably cleanerSame as get_it
Fit with flutter_blocStandard: BlocProvider(create: (_) => getIt<MyBloc>())No current production source pairing this combo — unverified—
Maturity4.7K likes, 1.7M downloads/30d [32]Not checked standaloneLeanBuilder since 2.12.0+ fixes slow builds [33]

gap provider and "no-package manual DI" were named candidates but not researched this round.

5. Secure storage — flutter_secure_storage

Runner-up: flutter_keychain. No realistic switch condition for an iOS-only app.
Criterionflutter_secure_storageflutter_keychain
Maintenance5.64M weekly downloads, verified publisher [9]Latest 3.0.1, far smaller footprint [14] (unverified at source)
iOS Keychain controlExposes accessibility classes directly incl. first_unlock [11][12]Not checked
Known pitfallv10→v11 cipher migration — pre-v10 data unreadable if migration step skipped [9][10]—

unverified iOS Keychain error codes -25308/-25291 around restart/background [13] — single-source, no second source found.

Architectural note: Keychain accessibility classes govern device-lock state, not the app's own biometric re-auth gate — RF03's 5-minute-timeout re-auth sits on top of, not inside, the storage package choice.

6. Biometrics — local_auth

Sole credible candidate — a hand-rolled platform-channel implementation was considered and rejected (duplicates the plugin, no documented upside for a solo timeline).
  • Verified flutter.dev publisher, 1.82M weekly downloads [22]
  • NSFaceIDUsageDescription required in Info.plist for Face ID; not required for Touch ID [23]
  • stickyAuth: true resumes in-flight auth on foreground return; false (default) fails immediately on backgrounding [24]. The 5-minute idle-timeout gate (RF03) itself is app-level logic, not plugin-provided.
  • Biometric lockout after repeated failures requires passcode entry to reset — no programmatic reset [23][25].

Cross-dimension insights

  • The codegen-avoidance pattern recurred independently three times (routing, DI, HTTP) despite each dimension being researched in isolation — weak evidence that "skip codegen for now" is the right default for this project's size, not one researcher's bias.
  • The abandoned-package trap was specific to local cache — no other category had a "popular but actually dead" result. A developer going by package-name familiarity alone would likely have picked isar/hive without knowing both are fork-dependent now.
  • Biometrics and secure storage are adjacent but distinct: local_auth gates access, flutter_secure_storage's Keychain accessibility class governs when stored data is readable relative to device-lock state. RF03 needs both wired together at the app layer; neither package solves the other's half.

Open questions

  • Cross-package integration friction (dio + flutter_secure_storage + get_it together) — not tested; resolve during F000 implementation, not more research.
  • go_router's version-to-version API stability complaint [31] — needs a direct read of flutter/packages GitHub issues.
  • flutter_secure_storage's iOS Keychain error codes on restart/background [13] — needs a direct GitHub issues search.
  • provider, manual-constructor DI, and GetX's router were never researched — no evidence either way if reconsidered.
  • riverpod-as-DI-under-flutter_bloc has no current production source evidencing the combination works — reasoned inference only.
